EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS

The Eagle Mountain City Council will hold public hearings on September 1, 2026, at 7:00 PM or as soon thereafter as business allows, in the Eagle Mountain City Council Chambers, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, Utah 84005.  The City Council will receive public comments concerning the following items:

Master Development Plan and Agreement Amendment:

-	Pinnacles 3 Parcel Master Development Plan and Agreement Amendment:  A request by Andy Flamm (with an associated Rezone and Future Land Use Amendment Set) to change the identification and zoning of three parcels of land (County Assessor Acct./Serial #s 59:034:0191, 59:034:0192 & 59:034:0193) being 2.48 acres, 6.04 acres and 5.24 acres respectively, all from Commercial Neighborhood to Agriculture and future land use setting/category from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Ag or AG/Rural Density.  
EMC Point of Contact: Senior Planner, Robert Hobbs: rhobbs@eaglemountian.gov.

Amendments to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code:

-	EMMC 17.60.130 - Retaining Wall Construction Standards: Consideration of an amendment to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.60.130. This amendment adds detailed design requirements for retaining walls, and includes clarification on building permit requirements, field inspections, and allowable retaining wall locations.  
EMC Point of Contact: City Engineer, Vince Hogge: vhogge@eaglemountain.gov.


THE PUBLIC IS INVITED TO PARTICIPATE IN ALL CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS.

Materials for public hearing items may be viewed within three days of the meeting on the city website and at the Eagle Mountain City Recorder's Office, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, UT, during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM. If you need special accommodation to participate in the meeting, please call the City Recorder's Office at 801.789.6611.  Open portions of the meeting can be viewed at www.eaglemountain.gov. 

Certificate of Posting
The undersigned, duly appointed City Recorder, does hereby certify that the above public hearing notice was posted on this 21th day of August, 2026, on the Eagle Mountain City bulletin boards, the Eagle Mountain City website, www.eaglemountain.gov, and posted to the Utah State public notice website http://www.utah.gov/pmn/index.html.

Lacie A. Messerly, City Recorder

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS


The Eagle Mountain City Council will hold public hearings on August 18, 2026, at 7:00 PM or as soon thereafter as business allows, in the Eagle Mountain City Council Chambers, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, Utah 84005. Adoption of the Final Budget for FY 2026-2027:

The final budget includes an increase to the property tax rate and will generate additional revenue to support public safety. 

The City Council reviewed the proposed Property Tax Impact Schedule on May 5, 2026, adopted the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Interim Budget on June 16, 2026, and held a Truth-in-Taxation public hearing on August 6, 2026, to receive public comment regarding the proposed property tax increase and its impact on property owners. The final budget will be the document that governs the expenditures for Fiscal Year 2026-2027. 
EMC Point of Contact: Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch: kruesch@eaglemountain.gov.

-	EMMC 16.25.040 - Final Plats: Consideration of an amendment to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.25.040, regarding street names and City maintained property on final plats.

	13.B.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Property Tax Increase Above the Certified Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026-2027.

BACKGROUND: Following the required Truth in Taxation public hearing, the City Council will consider approval of the proposed property tax increase above the certified tax rate for Fiscal Year 2026-2027, as required by Utah law. Approval of the proposed increase allows the City to incorporate the associated property tax revenue into the final Fiscal Year 2026-2027 budget.

	13.C.	RESOLUTION/PUBLIC HEARING - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Annual Budget Totaling $363,992,973.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Administrative Services Director Kimberly Ruesch) State statute requires taxing entities proposing a property tax increase above the certified tax rate to complete the Truth-in-Taxation process prior to adopting a final property tax rate and budget.  A Truth-in-Taxation public hearing was held on August 6, 2026, to receive public comment regarding the proposed property tax increase and the Council adopted a tax rate of 0.001500. This rate was a reduction from the interim budget proposed rate and reduces property tax revenue by $1,151,343.

14.	MID-VALLEY COMMUNITY REINVESTMENT PROJECT AREA

	14.A.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City and Eagle Mountain City for the Collection and Remittance of Incremental Property Taxes Collected from Property within the Mid-Valley Community Reinvestment Project Area.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Director of Legislative and Strategic Services, Evan Berrett): The Mid-Valley CRA encompasses approximately 53 acres currently under review for commercial retail development. The proposed Interlocal Agreement outlines the City's participation in tax increment financing for off-site project improvements and establishes the related administrative procedures and terms.

	14.B.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Mid-Valley CRA Participation Agreement between Eagle Mountain City, the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, and Terra Smith's Eagle Mountain, LLC.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Director of Legislative and Strategic Services, Evan Berrett): The Mid-Valley CRA encompasses approximately 53 acres currently under review for commercial retail development. The proposed resolution establishes the terms and conditions for the distribution and use of project area funds and addresses the obligations agreed upon by the participating parties through the negotiation process.

	14.C.	ORDINANCE - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Mid-Valley Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Director of Legislative and Strategic Services, Evan Berrett): The proposed ordinance adopts the Mid-Valley Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan as the official plan for the Mid-Valley Project Area. The Plan outlines the proposed development and establishes the framework for community reinvestment activities within the Project Area.

	14.D.	ORDINANCE - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah Approving the 5th Amendment to the Amended and Restated Overland Master Development Agreement.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by City Attorney, Marcus Draper) This item was approved at the March 25, 2026 Special City Council meeting. The parties have corrected some clerical errors in the document and have altered the language in sections 5.3, 5.4, and 5.6 for the City Council's review. The changes in the language relate to the infrastructure funding and directly incorporate the provisions of the participation agreement to ensure that there is no discrepancy between the agreements. It also adds some stronger language that reinforces existing language that the infrastructure improvements discussed in the agreement will be fully reimbursed.

NOTICE OF PROPOSED TAX INCREASE 
EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY is proposing to increase its property tax revenue. 

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY tax on a $488,000 residence would increase from
$142.25 to $456.28, which is $314.03 per year.

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY tax on a $488,000 business would increase from
$258.64 to $829.60, which is $570.96 per year.

If the proposed budget is approved, EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY would receive an additional $6,742,938 in property tax revenue per year as a result of the tax increase. If the proposed budget is approved, EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY would increase its property tax budgeted revenue by 220.88% above last year's property tax budgeted revenue excluding eligible new growth.

The EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY invites all concerned citizens to a public hearing for the purpose of hearing comments regarding the proposed tax increase and to explain the reasons for the proposed tax increase. You have the option to attend or participate in the public hearing in person or virtually.


PUBLIC HEARING

Date/Time:   8/6/2026 6:00 PM
Location:      Eagle Mountain City Hall Council Chambers 
                      1650 Stagecoach Run
                      Eagle Mountain

To obtain more information regarding the tax increase, citizens may contact the EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY at 801-789-6600 or visit https://eaglemountain.gov/ Instructions for virtual participation in the public hearing will be available at https://eaglemountain.gov/ no later than 24 hours before the public hearing is scheduled to begin.

EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS

The Eagle Mountain City Council will hold public hearings on August 4, 2026, at 7:00 PM or as soon thereafter as business allows, in the Eagle Mountain City Council Chambers, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, Utah 84005.  The City Council will receive public comments concerning the following items:

Transportation Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP):

-	Transportation Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) Update: The hearing is for adoption of an update to the Transportation Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) The City's Transportation Master Plan is intended to identify the needed transportation infrastructure needed to provide adequate service for the City's residents and businesses. This comprehensive transportation plan that must be developed and regularly maintained to combat the potential congestion caused by projected growth. NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS and PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD
Eagle Mountain City, Utah
U.S. Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program
Preparation of Proposed Program Year (PY) 2026 HUD CDBG Annual Action Plan
Eagle Mountain City will hold a Public Hearing on Tuesday, August 4, 2026 during a regularly scheduled council meeting at 7:00 p.m. in Council Chambers, at City Hall at 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain City, Utah 84005.
This notice is provided in compliance with the City's adopted Citizen Participation Plan, as required by 24 CFR (Code of Federal Regulations) 91. The Eagle Mountain City Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program is funded through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
Eagle Mountain City receives an annual allocation from the HUD CDBG program, as an Entitlement City. Eagle Mountain City (EMC) is preparing the required Program Year (PY) 2026 Annual Action Plan (AAP). The PY2026 allocation is currently estimated at $246,979, finalized with a grant agreement between EMC and HUD after HUD approval.
During the public hearing EMC staff, in accordance with HUD requirements, will outline goals and AAP projects under consideration for PY 2026 with CDBG funding.
Current funding outline includes:
Annual Allocation of $246,979 and Prior Year Resources of approximately $220,000, for a total of $466,979.
Project
Proposed Allocation
Housing Preservation and Development
$ 200,000
Public Services (capped at 15% of annual award)
$ 36,900
Public Facilities and Infrastructure Improvements
$ 180,879
PY 2026 Program Planning and Administration (capped at 20% of annual award)
$ 49,200
All amounts are estimates
The public is invited to attend this hearing and provide feedback on the EMC proposed AAP goals and projects.
NOTICE OF PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD
A public comment period on the proposed Annual Action Plan will begin on July 1, 2026 at 10:00 am MDT. Public comment period will close on August 4, 2026 at 7:00 pm MDT.
Comments received by the City on or before the end of the comment period will be forwarded to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Comments received after the comment period will not be considered.
A detailed account of the plans and activities associated with the CDBG program may be obtained by visiting the City's website at www.eaglemountain.gov, or by contacting Kiara Polee, Affordable Housing Coordinator, at telephone (801) 789-6700, or by email to kpolee@eaglemountain.gov.
Public notices regarding future public hearings for the 5-year Consolidated Plan, Annual Action Plans, and/or other HUD reports will be printed in a local newspaper of general circulation and posted online on the City's, website at www.eaglemountain.gov.
In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, individuals needing special accommodations should contact Taylor Draney at least five (5) days prior to the hearing. Individuals with hearing or speech impairments may dial 711 (Relay Utah).
Materials for public hearing items may be viewed within three days of the meeting on the city website and at the Eagle Mountain City Recorder's Office, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, UT, during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM. If you need special accommodation to participate in the meeting, please call the City Recorder's Office at 801.789.6611. Open portions of the meeting can be viewed at www.eaglemountain.gov.
The undersigned, duly appointed City Recorder, does hereby certify that the above agenda notice was posted on this 19th day of June, 2026, on the Eagle Mountain City bulletin boards, the Eagle Mountain City website www.eaglemountain.gov, posted to the Utah State public notice website http://www.utah.gov/pmn/index.html, and was emailed to at least one newspaper of general circulation within the jurisdiction of the public body.
Lacie A. Messerly
City Recorder
